subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw define an ACP skill-context contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes plus security/observability guarantees are allowed?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but implementation would add model-facing context across an external harness boundary where selection, redaction, audit metadata, default config, and Codex-native skill interaction require maintainer intent.

options.title: Start explicit-only with audit metadata
options.body: Add only an explicit per-call skill selector first, with redaction and observable selected ids/mode/render size/version or hash, and defer auto/default selection until the contract proves safe.

options.title: Design the full selector surface now
options.body: Keep the issue open for a broader design covering explicit, automatic, and default skill sets plus config and security review before any code path lands.

options.title: Decline core ACP skill injection
options.body: Close or redirect if maintainers want ACP children to rely on harness-native skills, ClawHub bundles, or explicit MCP/plugin bridges instead of OpenClaw core prompt injection.

recommendation.title: Start explicit-only with audit metadata
recommendation.body: Add only an explicit per-call skill selector first, with redaction and observable selected ids/mode/render size/version or hash, and defer auto/default selection until the contract proves safe.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP spawn and sessions_spawn history points most strongly to steipete for the product boundary and compatibility decision.
